summary: Round 2 re-validation. Both round-1 medium findings are fully addressed; no new critical mirages introduced by the edits. Verified ~50 claims across tech-spec including the new three-index Bot domain layer, the corrected EventService.logEvent call sites, and the new shadcn-vue Dialog prereq sub-step in Task 9. Three minor observations (not mirages): AVP mongosh check at line 430 only mentions the platform-wide index name and omits the new per-project index name (AC at line 478 already requires both), the 'matches existing email-send retry shape conceptually' aside at line 221 is a soft claim (EmailService has no actual Retry shape — fire-and-forget only), and useApiError signature in Task 9 description is colloquial (the composable takes no args; the returned function takes (error, contextKey)).

findings.claim: Tech-spec Agent Verification Plan, line 430: 'mongosh ... --eval "db.bots.getIndexes()" after backend boot in dev profile ... partial unique index telegramBotId_unique_connected present with filter { status: "CONNECTED" }'.
findings.reality: After round-2 edits Bot now declares THREE indexes including a new partial unique on (projectId) filtered to status=CONNECTED, named projectId_unique_connected (Data Models lines 279-282). The AVP mongosh check at line 430 only names telegramBotId_unique_connected and does not assert presence of the new projectId_unique_connected. AC item at line 478 already says 'Both partial unique indexes — telegramBotId_unique_connected and projectId_unique_connected — exist', so the requirement is captured at AC level — only the AVP smoke step lags. Implementer running the verification will likely add it, but the table row is incomplete.
findings.fix: Extend the AVP mongosh row to assert both partial unique indexes by name (telegramBotId_unique_connected AND projectId_unique_connected), or change the wording to '...the two partial unique indexes...' to match the AC.

findings.claim: Decision 11 rationale (line 221): '3 attempts is the platform default for transient external failures (matches existing email-send retry shape conceptually).'
findings.reality: EmailService (backend/src/main/java/com/botfunnel/email/EmailService.java) has no Retry.backoff / retryWhen / retry policy at all — sendAsync() is fire-and-forget on Schedulers.boundedElastic() with a single subscribe-and-log-on-error. The 'platform default for transient external failures' framing is conceptual rather than codified. Not a blocker — the rationale is internally coherent — but the appeal to an 'existing email-send retry shape' is misleading.
findings.fix: Soften the wording: drop the email-send analogy and instead frame the 3-attempt choice as a fresh design decision balanced against the frontend's ~35s ofetch timeout budget.

findings.reality: Actual useApiError() composable (frontend/composables/useApiError.ts:16) takes zero arguments and returns a function with signature resolveMessage(error, contextKey) — the context key is the SECOND positional arg of the returned function, not an arg to useApiError() itself. An implementer copying the literal call expression from tech-spec produces a wrong call shape (passes the context key to the wrong function). The intent is clear and the contextKey strings themselves are correct.
findings.fix: Update wording to 'Errors resolved via the function returned by useApiError(), invoked as resolve(error, "bot.connect" | "bot.disconnect" | "bot.testMessage")'.
